phase3_findings.description: import_bundle runs _plan (sqlglot parse and regenerate of every stored and incoming SQL pair via sql_key) directly on the event loop instead of through run_memory_call, blocking the HTTP server during imports and add_memories; no responsiveness test covers it.
The TokenError fallback of sql_key has no test (no tokenizer-failing input such as SELECT 'abc).
Public MemoryStore.set_groups accepts an empty sequence; ChromaDB metadata merge would keep the old groups. The grow-only rule lives only in a comment.
DedupEntry and _NewItem keep kind and payload as separate fields, so mismatched pairs can be built.
memory.md line 152 and transport.md line 121 describe one memory-worker call for the import and omit the new set_groups write path.
Changed _enforce_item_caps docstring names MemoryStore.iter_all as the import dedup check; the import now reads dedup_entries. Capped at Suggestion by the behavior-inert prose cap.
_both_paths only asserts direct hits appear in the tool result, never that out-of-scope questions are absent.
No test covers set_groups raising MemoryChangedDuringImportError when a record disappears mid-import, on any surface.
No test asserts the CLI prints the CSV dropped-groups Warning:.
record_groups silently returns [] for a tagged record with malformed memory_groups, while scope_filter treats it as tagged; export then re-import makes it visible to every rule set.
dedup_entries skips unreadable rows without counting or logging them, so their duplicates are saved again.

report:
## Verdict: REJECT (two checklist FAILs at or above the important threshold, plus one Important reviewer finding)

This PR is not ready to merge: `verify-memory` does not refuse a golden file whose schema docs carry `groups`, `add_memories` writes valid items while an invalid item in the same call names an unknown group, and the import's duplicate check parses SQL on the server's event loop.

Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

### 🔴 Critical

- VC-72: FAIL (critical) — `sqllens verify-memory` exits non-zero before running any case when its golden file has an item carrying `groups`, and the message names that item. [src/sqllens/eval/golden.py] — fix the code, or have the issue author amend this criterion

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Criterion 16 (criteria.json, graded with the file as it is a valid list): verify-memory must exit non-zero before running any case when its golden file has an item carrying `groups`, naming that item. cli.py:650-653 calls load_golden before run_verification and exits 1 on BundleFormatError, and golden.py:58-63 raises it naming the index and question for an sql_pairs pair with groups. That path conforms. But golden.py:55-56 returns [] when bundle.sql_pairs is None, before any groups check, and the loop at 58 only inspects sql_pairs.pairs. The memory schema lets schema_docs items carry `groups` (memory/schema.py:105-112, SchemaDoc.groups), and the loader docstring (golden.py:36-37) says schema_docs are ignored. Counterexample: a golden JSON with sql_pairs plus a schema_docs item with groups: load_golden returns the cases, no error, and verify-memory runs the cases (exit 0 possible) instead of refusing. A schema_docs-only file with groups gives the generic 'golden file is empty' error (cli.py:654-661), which does not name the item. Alternatives split: the `pair.groups is not None` check -> covers only sql_pairs items; schema_docs items are a departure inside the trigger (criterion says 'an item'). No sibling criterion narrows this.

  </details>

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. `src/sqllens/memory/importer.py` line 198: `import_bundle` calls `_plan(bundle, existing)` directly in the coroutine, not through `run_memory_call`. `_plan` runs `sqlglot.parse` and `.sql()` through `sql_key` on every stored SQL pair and every incoming pair, each up to 10,000 characters. On a large store or bundle this blocks the HTTP server's event loop for `import_memory`, `add_memories` and `sqllens import-memory`, and no test covers responsiveness while `_plan` runs. (raised by 1/6 agents)

- VC-4: FAIL (important) — An import naming an unknown group, or any group with no rule-set file, is refused before anything is written or cleared, even with --clear, across CLI, import tool, add tool. [docs/external/managing-memory.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Main paths hold: importer.py:193-195 import_bundle raises UnknownMemoryGroupsError before _baseline (the only clear, line 197) or any write; configured_groups (importer.py:75-78) returns frozenset() when cfg.rule_sets.loaded is None; the CLI (cli.py:491-498) refuses before the --clear confirm and MemoryStore open; the import tool (server.py:582-588) and add tool (server.py:815-826) pass known_groups and map the error to isError; the error text (schema.py:137-143) lists every unknown group. Counterexample for the add tool: admin.add_memories (admin.py:262-294) validates each item first and drops failing ones into per-row errors BEFORE building the bundle passed to import_bundle. A call with one valid pair plus an item such as {question:'', sql:'select 1', groups:['bogus']} (fails SqlPair validation) names an unknown group, yet unknown_groups only sees the valid pairs, so no refusal happens; the valid pair is written and the response is a per-row validation error that does not name the unknown group. This contradicts the absolute 'an import naming an unknown group ... is refused before anything is written ... the error names each unknown group' for the add tool. Narrow reach (the offending item itself is never stored), hence important rather than critical.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (10)

<details><summary>10 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/memory/importer.py` lines 50-66: the `TokenError` fallback of `sql_key` has no test. The tests cover several statements, a parse failure and `RecursionError`, but no input that makes the tokenizer fail, such as `SELECT 'abc`. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` lines 229-257: the public `MemoryStore.set_groups` accepts an empty sequence, and because ChromaDB merges metadata on update the record would keep its old groups. The rule that groups only grow is stated only in a comment. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` lines 125-136 (`DedupEntry`) and `src/sqllens/memory/importer.py` lines 99-103 (`_NewItem`): the record kind and its payload are separate fields, so a mismatched pair can be built. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `docs/internal/agent/memory.md` line 152 and `docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md` line 121: both still describe one memory-worker call for the import and leave out the new `run_memory_call(store.set_groups, plan.updates)` write path. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `src/sqllens/memory/io.py` line 81: the changed docstring of `_enforce_item_caps` calls `MemoryStore.iter_all` the import dedup check, but the import now reads `MemoryStore.dedup_entries`. (raised by 1/6 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: docstring of _enforce_item_caps only; making it true changes no branch; git grep for 'import dedup check' finds only io.py:81, no tool or agent reads it; internal docstring not printed -->
6. `tests/unit/test_memory_groups.py` (`_both_paths`): the tool-path check only asserts that direct search hits appear in the tool result. It never asserts that out-of-scope questions are absent from it. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` (`set_groups`, `MemoryChangedDuringImportError`): no test covers a record that disappears between the baseline read and the group write, on the CLI, `import_memory` or `add_memories`. (raised by 1/6 agents)
8. `src/sqllens/memory/exporter.py`: no test checks that `sqllens export-memory --format csv` prints the dropped-groups `Warning:`; only `export_bundle(...).warnings` is asserted. (raised by 1/6 agents)
9. `src/sqllens/_memory_groups.py` lines 42-51: `record_groups` returns `[]` without logging for a record marked tagged whose `memory_groups` is missing or malformed, while `scope_filter` still treats it as tagged. Listing, stats and export then report it as untagged, and a re-import makes it visible to every rule set. (raised by 1/6 agents)
10. `src/sqllens/memory/store.py` (`dedup_entries`): rows whose `args_json` does not parse, or whose fields are not strings, are skipped without a count or log, so a duplicate of such a row is saved again as new. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A rule-set file whose rule sets carry `memory_groups` loads with `format_version = 1`. A rule-set file with no `memory_groups` anywhere loads as before this change. A `memory_groups` that is empty, holds a duplicate, or holds a non-string is refused at load like any other invalid rule-set field.
- [ ] While a rule-set file is configured, a `query_database` request under rule set S gets, from both the `search_saved_correct_tool_uses` tool and the automatic system-prompt memory context, only records that are untagged or share at least one group with S's `memory_groups`. A tagged record whose groups S does not list is never returned to a request under S.
- [ ] While a rule-set file is configured, a memory search with an empty group list (the request's rule set lists no `memory_groups`, or no rule-set selection is available to the search) gets only untagged records from both memory paths.
- [ ] A memory search under rule set S returns an in-scope record that clears the similarity threshold even when more records than the search's result limit, all outside S's groups, score higher.
- [ ] A record stored before the upgrade, while it remains untagged, is retrieved after the upgrade by requests under every rule set, with no re-import or migration step.
- [ ] Without a rule-set file, memory retrieval returns tagged and untagged records alike, as before this change.
- [ ] `sqllens verify-memory` run with `--rule-set S` retrieves memory exactly as a `query_database` request under S does.
- [ ] `sqllens import-memory`, the `import_memory` tool and the `add_memories` tool accept an optional `groups` list (non-empty, distinct strings) on each SQL pair and schema doc. An empty or duplicate-holding `groups` is a validation error.
- [ ] An import through any of those three surfaces that names a group no loaded rule set's `memory_groups` lists leaves the store unchanged, with nothing written and, for `sqllens import-memory --clear`, nothing deleted. The CLI exits non-zero and the tools return `isError: true`, and the message names every unknown group. With no rule-set file configured, any import that names a group is refused this way.
- [ ] An imported item that duplicates an existing record or an earlier item of the same import creates no second record and sets the groups of every record it matches this way: a tagged item onto a tagged record gives the union of both; a tagged item onto an untagged record gives the item's groups; an untagged item leaves the record's groups as they were. A duplicate that changed the record's groups is counted as updated, and one that changed nothing as a skipped duplicate. The updated count is shown as `updated=<n>` in the `sqllens import-memory` summary line, in the `import_memory` tool's report, and as `updated_count` in the `add_memories` result. A dry run reports the same counts without writing.
- [ ] Duplicate detection compares `sql` texts with sqlglot under the MySQL dialect: two texts match when each parses into exactly one statement and both regenerate to the same SQL, with string literals and identifiers keeping their case, so `WHERE region = 'EU'` and `where region = 'eu'` do not match while `SELECT a FROM t` and `select a\n  from t` do. When sqlglot raises any exception on either `sql` text while parsing or regenerating (`ParseError`, `TokenError` and `RecursionError` included), or the text parses into no statement or more than one, the two match only when their texts are identical after trimming leading and trailing whitespace, so re-importing the same file still saves nothing new. `question` texts match after collapsing whitespace and ignoring case, and `content` texts match as before this change.
- [ ] For a store in which no two records duplicate each other under the match rule, exporting it to JSON with `sqllens export-memory` or the `export_memories` tool and importing the result into an empty store recreates every record the export wrote, with the same groups, untagged records staying untagged, when every group the export names is listed in a loaded rule set's `memory_groups`. An export naming a group no rule set lists is refused on import like any other unknown group.
- [ ] A CSV export of a store holding at least one tagged record returns `lossy: true` from `export_memories`, and `sqllens export-memory` prints a `Warning:`. Both state how many records' groups were dropped. A CSV import never changes an existing record's groups.
- [ ] `list_memories` and `get_memory` return each record's groups. While a rule-set file is configured, `get_memory_stats` returns the count of tagged records none of whose groups appears in any rule set's `memory_groups`; without a rule-set file that count is 0.
- [ ] `get_access_rules` returns each rule set's `memory_groups`.
- [ ] `sqllens verify-memory` exits non-zero before running any case when its golden file has an item carrying `groups`, and the message names that item.
- [ ] The change leaves these unchanged: with a rule-set file configured, the agent has neither `save_question_tool_args` nor `save_text_memory`; and the memory admin tools (`list_memories`, `get_memory`, `export_memories`, `get_memory_stats`, `delete_memory`, `clear_memories`, `add_memories`) and `import_memory` act on every record for any caller, without regard to rule sets.
- [ ] `docs/external/rule-sets.md` documents `memory_groups` in the file reference and replaces the "Memory is shared by every rule set" limit with the group rule, still stating that the memory admin tools are not limited by rule sets and that SQL Lens trusts `_meta`.
- [ ] `docs/external/managing-memory.md` documents the bundle `groups` field, the unknown-group refusal, how duplicates combine groups, and that CSV carries no groups. Its paragraph beginning "Duplicate entries are skipped automatically" states the new match rule (SQL compared by sqlglot with literal and identifier case kept, exact text when the SQL does not parse) and that a duplicate which changes a record's groups counts as updated.
- [ ] `docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md` and `docs/internal/agent/memory.md` describe group-filtered retrieval. No doc or code comment states that memory is shared by every rule set as a fact; today that claim appears at least in `docs/external/rule-sets.md` (the "Nothing is saved to memory" and "Memory is shared by every rule set" bullets), `docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md` and the rule-set write-gate comment in `src/sqllens/agent/factory.py`.
- [ ] The `chromadb` lower bound in `pyproject.toml` admits only releases that support list-valued metadata and the `$contains` filter on it, and that evaluate the metadata filter the retrieval uses the way 1.5.9 does for a record missing the filtered key.

checklist.claim: An import naming an unknown group, or any group with no rule-set file, is refused before anything is written or cleared, even with --clear, across CLI, import tool, add tool.

checklist.verify_hint: Trace import_bundle in src/sqllens/memory/importer.py and import_memory in src/sqllens/cli.py with --clear and a bundle naming one unknown group; check configured_groups returns empty without a rule-set file
checklist.evidence: Main paths hold: importer.py:193-195 import_bundle raises UnknownMemoryGroupsError before _baseline (the only clear, line 197) or any write; configured_groups (importer.py:75-78) returns frozenset() when cfg.rule_sets.loaded is None; the CLI (cli.py:491-498) refuses before the --clear confirm and MemoryStore open; the import tool (server.py:582-588) and add tool (server.py:815-826) pass known_groups and map the error to isError; the error text (schema.py:137-143) lists every unknown group. Counterexample for the add tool: admin.add_memories (admin.py:262-294) validates each item first and drops failing ones into per-row errors BEFORE building the bundle passed to import_bundle. A call with one valid pair plus an item such as {question:'', sql:'select 1', groups:['bogus']} (fails SqlPair validation) names an unknown group, yet unknown_groups only sees the valid pairs, so no refusal happens; the valid pair is written and the response is a per-row validation error that does not name the unknown group. This contradicts the absolute 'an import naming an unknown group ... is refused before anything is written ... the error names each unknown group' for the add tool. Narrow reach (the offending item itself is never stored), hence important rather than critical.
